Updated: 2026-10-19 13:07 CEST. Proof checkpoint: `904d230ff`.
Verified start: `1862b2fc6`. Source main remains `184bba662`.
Read `lean/notes-current-native-edge-child-retention.md`.
Actual causal History now derives the same earlier edge writer with
native returned-cell retention from its captured body return into the
checked reader. Its actual makeEdge and child-Walk suffixes retain the
selected child return into that same reader. Surviving children cannot

bound on the generated output child and needs no positivity premise.

Origin view remains separate. Stored Mu winners and current callbacks
are not identified. No native History is assigned to the physical view.

# Native child writers through historical edge calls

Checked: 2026-10-19. Proof checkpoint: `904d230ff`.
Verified start: `1862b2fc6`. Source main: `184bba662`.
Evidence: `restart-evidence/20261019-native-edge-child-retention/`.

This checkpoint supplies the missing native interval from an earlier edge
writer to its checked reader. It then derives the selected surviving
child's exact returned node cell and writer at that same reader. It covers
cold calls and warm cache hits. It assumes no History at an internal active
child entry.

## Same captured edge writer

`SourceCurrentNativeEdgeWriterRetention.Written` retains one actual earlier
edge-body execution. Its existential contains the same Checked entry and
return, fuel, Good entry, ready request, evaluating owner, body trace,
protected finish and both heap-growth facts. It also retains

`Retained capturedBodyAfter.native reader.native`.

This relation belongs to that same captured body return. A second unrelated
writer existential would not supply the required interval. `Written.forget`
gives the older heap-growth receipt.

`edge_writers` derives the stronger receipt from actual causal History and
an exact returned edge cell at the reader. Its History induction covers
logical empty startup, physical advancement and actual clean checked
traces. The actual edge finish records the writer. Later operations retain
that writer's native cells. The theorem adds no future-success premise.

## Actual selected child

`SourceCurrentNativeWriterChildRetention.live` inverts that same edge body.
The all-child survival premise excludes its sentinel `[Empty]` branch.
The accepted branch retains the actual ordered child Walk and complete
output row fields. The actual makeEdge suffix derives native retention
from the child-Walk return into the captured edge-body return. Composition
with the stronger writer interval reaches the chosen native reader.

`child` selects the exact same index in both original input rows. It
retains the actual child Trace, Good endpoints, heap growth and

`Retained actualChildAfter.native reader.native`.

The actual remaining Walk supplies the first native interval. No heap-only
relation is used to infer native cells.

`returned` applies the existing actual-request Forwarded producer with
History at the final checked reader. A direct unresolved request returns
literal Empty. The surviving selected child is not Empty. This excludes
the direct arm and derives the child's exact returned node cell and
`NativeWriterReadyRetention.Written` at that reader. It needs no child
Origin, closedness, positivity or semantic result law.

## Surviving row and separate physical view

`SourceCurrentNativeReaderChildRetention.rows_returned` starts from an
actual completed compileRows trace, Good entry, final-reader History and
native retention from the actual compiler return to that reader. It keeps
the selected canonical output row and chosen child index. Actual ordered
pair enumeration derives both original input row indices.

The exact selected edge-call return travels through its actual row-Walk
suffix and makeNode suffix. The reader History then supplies the earlier
edge writer with its stronger native interval. This also covers a warm
selected edge call whose current execution has no child Walk.

Canonical survival derives that none of the output row's children is
literal Empty. The selected child therefore gets its actual paired call,
native retention, Forwarded receipt, returned cell and strong node writer.
The row keeps its full symbol and conjoined constraint.

`ordinary` consumes a captured returned node cell, actual ordinary branch,
and a complete row Origin at a separate physical view. It derives the
same returned-child contract. Both original input children have strictly
smaller mass than their respective original node operands. This places no
mass bound on the generated output child. It needs no positivity premise.

All native cells, History and writers belong to the captured checked
reader. The physical view may differ. No native History is assigned to it.
The stored Mu unfolding and captured writer callback remain distinct.

## Constructed check and verification

The constructed fixture builds an actual positive ordinary query with two
nonempty leaf children. It derives its cold Trace and reader History.
An explicit second requestEdge execution is a two-step warm cache hit.
The check derives the stronger edge receipt, its older projection and the
selected child's retained call, Forwarded receipt, returned cell and writer.
It assumes no desired writer receipt and no internal child-entry History.
It does not claim that a recursive or changed child is exercised.

Eight production public declarations and one constructed declaration pass
complete statement, proof and standard-axiom checks. All eight printer
settings are retained. The checks reject omitted proof text and nonstandard
axioms. Three production and one constructed strict logs are empty.
The first reader strict attempt retains its unused-instance warnings and
is not selected. The corrected second attempt has an empty log.

Root observed the exact default full-audit-1 execution handle 41241 return
exit zero. The build ran 3462 jobs and checked 73854 axiom dependencies.
The sole warning is the older unused inputs binding in
InternedFreshOrdinaryClosedCompletion. All selected runs retain effective
4 GiB maximum/high memory limits and zero swap.

## Remaining work

The ordinary child native-provenance gap is closed for these contracts.
The next source argument must compose the child's writer with the actual
remaining PathOrigin. Reference bindings and Mu publications still need
the required source ancestry. A stored Mu winner is not identified with
an arbitrary current callback. No new global renewal bound, active-owner
exclusion, general completion, repeated-pass convergence or Haskell
correspondence follows from these results.

The constructed root-language and exact returned size-query guarantees
remain unchanged. The full-library target remains active, including
generation, probability and external interfaces. The upstream ordered
cursor, prepared-template exclusion and shared subsumption worklist still
need implementation proofs. No Haskell source changes in this checkpoint.
Root FINDINGS retains the Haskell repair registry first. Publication awaits
the pending direct approval. No push or board write is attempted.

Checked against the live theorem statements on 2026-10-19.
Read `notes-current-native-edge-child-retention.md` for the latest checkpoint.

In simple technical English: fresh construction always finishes in the
Lean model. Under the stated guard conditions, its result represents
exactly the finite trees specified by its expression. A completed supported
modeled root reduction with empty inherited constraints preserves that
exact language.
The root theorem derives the logical startup cache and guard facts.
Field allocation, validity, guard coverage and numeric resources remain
explicit. General termination and Haskell correspondence remain open.

Actual causal edge History now retains native cells from the same earlier
edge-body return into the captured checked reader. Its actual makeEdge
and child-Walk suffixes retain the selected surviving child return.
Forwarded excludes the unresolved direct arm because that child is not
Empty. The child's exact returned node cell and writer therefore belong
to the same reader, with no History at an internal active child entry.
The ordinary-origin adapter retains both original input row indices,
the selected child index, full row fields and strict original input-child
mass bounds. It bounds no generated output child. This closes the
ordinary child native-provenance gap for these contracts. Composition with
the remaining PathOrigin and source ancestry through reference bindings
and Mu publications still need proof. Whole-event projection and the
global renewal bound remain separate open obligations.
